paragraphs.text: And they truly build themselves therein a strong dwelling place, if becoming, by humility, as little children in their own sight, they are nourished in the sublimity of Christ; if they feel themselves to be weak, and give up the confidence of their mind, to be cherished by the lofty humility of the Redeemer Who is known to them; if they seek not after things below; if they pass over, with the flight of their heart, every thing which passes away. Let us behold the eagle building itself the nest of hope in high places. He says; Our conversation is in heaven. And again; Who hath raised us up together, and hath made us sit together in heavenly places.
paragraphs.author: Pacian of Barcelona
paragraphs.work: Morals on the Book of Job, Book 31, Section 94

paragraphs.text: He has his rest in high places, because in truth he fixes his thought on things above. He wishes not to degrade his mind to the lowest objects, he wishes not, by the baseness of human conversation, to dwell in things below. Paul was, perhaps, then confined in prison, when he was witnessing that he was sitting together with Christ in heavenly places. But he was there, where he had already fixed his ardent mind, not there, where the sluggish flesh was still necessarily detaining him.
paragraphs.author: Pacian of Barcelona
paragraphs.work: Morals on the Book of Job, Book 31, Section 94

paragraphs.text: Kenite means "possession." And who are those who possess present things but the ones who are skilled in the study of secular wisdom? They are those who, by their study, truly build themselves a sturdy dwelling, if they make themselves into little children with humility and are nourished by Christ's grandeur. They sense that they are weak, and [they] place their trust in the exalted humility of the Redeemer they have acknowledged and foster that trust. They do not seek out the heights. They transcend, by the flight of their hearts, everything that is passing.
paragraphs.author: Paterius
paragraphs.work: EXPOSITION OF THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENT, Numbers 22

paragraphs.text: Let us ponder the holy man, how he builds his nest on the rock. For he says, "our conversation is in heaven," and "who revived and made us be seated in heaven." This holy man has his nest in the cliffs, because he took counsel on high. He does not want to cast his mind down into the depths; he does not want to dwell in the depths through dejected human conversation. Paul was imprisoned when he attested that he was seated with Christ in heaven. He was where he had fixed his mind, already afire, and not where sluggish flesh retained him by force.
paragraphs.author: Paterius
paragraphs.work: EXPOSITION OF THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENT, Numbers 22

paragraphs.text: But after these things Balaam concludes the discourse of his prophecy in these words, saying: "And having taken up his parable, he said: Oh, oh, who shall live, when God shall do these things? And he shall come forth out of the hands of the Kittim, and they shall afflict Asshur, and they shall afflict the Hebrews, and they themselves shall likewise perish." That Balaam is said to speak through each detail by way of a parable strikes shame into the reader, lest in these things that are said he should think anything said not as in a parable, but according to the letter.
paragraphs.author: Origen of Alexandria

paragraphs.text: He says, then: "Oh, oh, who shall live, when God shall do these things?" Here he names not this common life, but that life which is according to God, and this is what he says: that, when all these things shall come to pass, when a star shall arise out of Jacob, and a man shall rise up out of Israel and shall destroy Amalek and shall bring his seed to perdition, that is, when Christ shall come and shall destroy the worship of idols and shall subject the power of all the demons, who shall be so blessed, so happy, as to see these things? that is, who shall perceive and understand and believe that God has done these things thus? "And they shall come forth out of the hands of the Kittim, and they shall afflict the Assyrians." The Kittim are interpreted "the stroke of the end." These, therefore, who, being converted to the Lord and instructed by Christ, escape the stroke which shall come upon the impious at the end of the age, they themselves shall afflict the Assyrians, that is, these, for whom, being set in the contest of piety, God shall crush Satan under their feet, they themselves shall afflict the Assyrians, namely the nation of demons.
paragraphs.author: Origen of Alexandria

paragraphs.text: For they shall tread upon serpents and scorpions, and upon all the power of the enemy, and shall afflict them. "And they shall afflict the Hebrews, and they themselves shall likewise perish." The Hebrews are interpreted "those passing over." This same people, therefore, is also called Hebrew, because it passes over from Egypt to the land of promise, from darkness to light, from death to life. But since these things, as we have said, cannot be obtained without a contest nor without a great struggle, as one set in the contest he now afflicts, now is afflicted, and now smites the adversary, now is himself beaten by the adversary.
paragraphs.author: Origen of Alexandria

paragraphs.text: Therefore the Assyrians themselves also shall afflict the Hebrews, that is, the people of God, just as they are afflicted by them; but they themselves, that is the Assyrians, when they shall have done these things and when they shall have poured out all their strength upon afflicting the Hebrews, immediately they themselves also shall perish.
paragraphs.author: Origen of Alexandria

paragraphs.text: As for what he says, then: "And they shall afflict the Hebrews, and they themselves shall likewise perish," it is not to be taken as though the Assyrians shall perish together with the Hebrews; but "likewise," that is, immediately as they shall have done these things, as they shall have afflicted the Hebrews, they themselves also shall perish; for the Greek word puts "likewise" for "immediately." This, therefore, shall be the end of all things, that even Asshur, to whom were handed over those who were transgressing from the people of God, either unto the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit might be saved, or that they might learn not to blaspheme, shall himself also perish at the hands of Him who has the power to destroy in Gehenna.
paragraphs.author: Origen of Alexandria

paragraphs.text: For it shall be said to them by the just judge: "Go into the eternal fire, which God prepared for the devil and his angels." There, therefore, Asshur shall perish. And indeed one sheep too out of the hundred sheep once perished, but this sheep the good shepherd, leaving the ninety and nine in the mountains and descending to this valley of ours, the valley of tears, and seeking it, found it and, having laid it upon his shoulders, carried it back and joined it to that number which in the passages above remained saved.
paragraphs.author: Origen of Alexandria

paragraphs.text: But this Asshur, who is said to be about to perish at the end of all things, I know not whether he can ever either be sought or be found; for he perishes not by error, but by judgment, nor moved by a lapse, but hardened by perseverance. For as to what is written: "I will kill and I will make to live, I will lead down into hell and I will bring back," I know not whether it looks generally to all or only to those whom the deception of the devil caused to be led down into death.
paragraphs.author: Origen of Alexandria

paragraphs.text: Let these things too concerning the last prophecy of Balaam be said by us according to our strength, which, because of the difficulty of the passages, it has seemed good to unfold rather with the pen of one explaining than of one delivering a formal discourse. For what does it matter, provided that all things be said unto edification and all things be done unto the glory of God? Who is blessed unto the ages of ages. Amen.
paragraphs.author: Origen of Alexandria
